message.content:
The function `ccm_finish_reduced` takes a `tag_len` parameter from the caller and uses it in a `memcpy` operation to copy data from a fixed-size buffer `full_tag` (which is 16 bytes) into the destination buffer `tag`. 

The vulnerability is a buffer overflow (specifically a stack-based buffer overflow if `tag_len` is larger than 16, or a heap/stack overflow of the destination `tag` if `tag_len` is larger than the allocated size of `tag`). Since `tag_len` is provided by the caller and is not validated against the size of the source buffer `full_tag` (16 bytes), a caller can provide a `tag_len` greater than 16, causing `memcpy` to read past the end of `full_tag`. Even if `tag_len` is within the bounds of `tag`, the lack of a check against the source buffer size `16` makes line 10 the site of the memory corruption/out-of-bounds read.

Answer: 10
